record.what_it_does: Web data platform: proxies, Web Unlocker, SERP API, scrapers, datasets, cloud browsers.
record.auth_notes: The REST API takes an account API key, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <API key>'. Native (proxy) access uses a proxy-protocol username and password. Bright Data has no OAuth, so each end user supplies their own key. Some account-management calls require Admin or Ops roles. The hosted MCP takes the token as a URL query parameter.
record.access_notes: Accounts are self-serve and an API key comes from account settings. The Web Unlocker pricing page shows a Free Tier of 5K requests a month, then pay-as-you-go at $1.5 per 1K requests. Neither pricing page I opened says whether a credit card is needed. Residential proxy zones created after July 7, 2026 need KYC approval (per a search-result summary of the docs; I did not open that page), but the scraping and Unlocker APIs are not gated.
record.api_breadth_notes: The API covers Web Unlocker and SERP (POST /request), Scraper API (sync and async trigger, snapshots), Scraper Studio, Dataset Marketplace, Browser API, and Functions. Account Management covers zones: list all and active zones, zone info, add and remove zones, and available countries. I could not get a full endpoint count, and the total may be near the 50-operation threshold. The official MCP server exposes 31 tools.
record.mcp_notes: The hosted server is https://mcp.brightdata.com/mcp?token=YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE. The local server is the npm package @brightdata/mcp (GitHub repo brightdata/brightdata-mcp). It exposes 31 tools.
record.blocker_notes: Nothing blocks a build. Each user brings an API key because there is no OAuth, and usage is billed to that user's account. Webhooks are per-job delivery callbacks: Bright Data POSTs results to an endpoint you set on the trigger, with an optional auth_header. They are not account-level event subscriptions.

evidence.quote: This <token> is your API key, which is required for every API request.
Use your Bright Data API Key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
Bright Data sends a POST request to that URL with the scraped data once the job completes.
